nodes.question: Is the paper visibly inside the cup, with evidence it has been stuffed into it rather than merely resting nearby or on the rim?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the image shows the paper placed inside the cup and visibly stuffed into it. Fail if the paper is only nearby or on the rim, or the image shows no progress toward placing it inside. Unknown if the image does not provide enough evidence to determine whether it is inside and stuffed.
nodes.binding: Assess only the requested paper-in-cup edit, using the image evidence; unrelated edits do not count as progress.

nodes.question: Does the image provide enough evidence to determine whether the paper has been stuffed into the cup?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the image clearly resolves whether the paper is inside the cup and stuffed into it. Fail if the image clearly shows it is not stuffed into the cup. Unknown if visibility or ambiguity prevents a determination; retain this as unresolved rather than inferring completion or absence.
nodes.binding: Use only visible evidence of the paper’s placement relative to the cup; do not treat proximity or contact with the rim alone as proof of stuffing.

nodes.question: Does the image show the paper stuffed inside the cup?
nodes.criteria: Combine the supports under the frozen target: complete only when the paper is visibly inside the cup and evidence shows it has been stuffed into it; absent only when there is no progress toward that requested change; partial when there is some progress but the target is not complete. Unrelated edits are not progress. If required evidence remains insufficient or unresolved, report unknown rather than assuming complete, partial, or absent.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

fulfillment: The node’s current binding is malformed and underspecified: it contains a placeholder and asks only whether the paper is stuffed inside the cup, while the executable criteria must distinguish complete, partial progress, absent progress, and unresolved evidence. Repair the typed binding so it faithfully anchors the requested change to the instruction and preserves those distinctions. In particular, do not equate “not visibly inside” with “no progress”: inspect the edited image against the source for any observable movement toward putting the paper into the cup, and reserve absent for evidence of no progress; use partial if there is progress without completion and unknown if evidence is insufficient. Here, the edited image appears to show a hand holding a printed card/paper near a round object, not clearly the source paper and cup, so the supports’ confident claim that it is paper over a cup is not well grounded. Treat object identity and cup visibility as evidence questions, not assumptions; avoid converting this ambiguity into a confident absent judgment. The traces are valid and queried with no transport or dependency failure, but both supports share the same upstream observation, so their agreement is not independent corroboration. Preserve the frozen target and required checks rather than changing criteria merely to match the reference label.
s2: Repair the malformed placeholder binding and make the node assess the requested edit against the source, not merely whether the paper is currently inside the cup. Require evidence that the edited object is the source paper and that the round object is the source cup before making a confident placement judgment. The edited image appears to show a printed card near a reddish round object, unlike the source’s white paper and blue cup; identity and cup visibility are therefore unresolved, not proof of either progress or absence. Preserve the rubric’s distinctions: pass only for completed stuffing, fail only when visible evidence establishes no requested progress, partial for observable progress short of completion, and unknown when identity, visibility, or placement cannot be determined. Do not infer progress from proximity alone or infer no progress solely from non-completion. The traces are valid and queried, so this is a visual grounding and criterion/binding issue, not a transport or dependency failure; the shared upstream observation is not independent corroboration. Keep the frozen target and required checks rather than tuning the criterion to the reference label.
s1: Replace the malformed placeholder binding with a typed, source-grounded assessment of the requested paper-into-cup edit. The current trace’s confident “paper over a cup” interpretation is not supported by the images: the edit shows a hand holding a blue printed card near a reddish round object, while the source shows white paper and a blue cup. Treat identity and cup visibility as unresolved evidence questions, not established facts. Preserve the rubric’s distinctions: completed placement, observable but incomplete progress, no progress only when evidence supports that conclusion, and unresolved when identity or placement cannot be determined. Do not equate failure to complete with absence of progress, infer progress from proximity alone, or tune the criterion to the reference label. The trace was valid and queried with no transport or dependency failure; this is a visual-grounding and criterion/binding issue.

rejected_diagnostics.semantic_rejection: The support checks do not provide sufficient evidence for the requested distinction between paper stuffed inside the cup and paper merely placed inside it. s1 asks for visible evidence of stuffing, but its criteria treat placement inside plus visible stuffing as a pass without defining what evidence establishes stuffing; s2 repeats that same ambiguity rather than checking a distinct, finer condition. The fulfillment readout then relies on those supports to decide completion, partial progress, or absence, so it cannot faithfully distinguish incomplete progress from no progress. The program also makes the fulfillment node active on every s2 status, including unknown, despite its parent being a support check; this is not itself a valid basis for resolving the missing evidence.

The support checks do not establish the requested extent. s3 only tests whether any portion of the paper enters the cup, while s1 and s2 both ask whether it is stuffed inside and do not separately establish a clear completion condition. The fulfillment rule therefore cannot reliably distinguish complete stuffing from partial entry: it treats s3 entry plus failure to establish completion as partial, but s1/s2 may fail or remain unknown without proving incompleteness. This leaves the required complete/partial/absent distinctions under-supported.

The support checks do not provide sufficient evidence for the requested relation. s1 can pass on the broad observation that paper is inside and appears stuffed, but cup_identity only checks whether the source cup can be matched to an edited object; it does not establish that the paper is inside that identified cup. s2 is nested under cup_identity but depends only on s1, so it can assess the relation without the identity evidence that fulfillment says is required. The readout’s identity gate therefore cannot reliably ground the placement evidence, and its fallback to “other saved evidence” does not resolve this gap.
